summary: Every Nigerian state runs its own scholarship or bursary board, usually for indigenes of that state. Awards range from a yearly bursary (for example, Lagos lists ₦200,000 for undergraduates and ₦300,000–₦400,000 for Master's/PhD) to occasional fully funded overseas scholarships. Winners are indigenes who prove their state of origin, apply in the short window with complete documents, and — for merit awards — pass a test or interview.
lookfor: Proof you are an indigene: certificate of origin / LGA identification letter (Lagos also asks for LASSRA and an Oba/LG letter)
Current enrolment in a recognised (often public) institution, matching your NIN and school records
For merit awards: a high CGPA (e.g. Lagos merit 3.5/5; Akwa Ibom indigent-student scheme 3.5/5) and a good test or interview score
For need-based awards: evidence of financial need, e.g. a letter on parents' occupation
Complete, authentic documents submitted inside the window — fake documents lead to disqualification
cycle: Each board sets its own dates. Examples: Lagos 2025/26 bursary ran 19 January–27 February 2026 on portal.lagosscholarship.org; Akwa Ibom runs a year-round bursary portal on bursary.akwaibomstate.gov.ng. For 2026/27, many boards open after schools resume (roughly November–March) — check your state's official site monthly.

eligibility.q: Do you know your state of origin and Local Government Area, and can you get a certificate of origin from that LGA?
eligibility.no: Visit your LGA secretariat with your birth certificate and a parent's details to get one. Without it you cannot prove indigeneship.

eligibility.q: Are you currently admitted to or studying in a recognised Nigerian or overseas institution at the level the scheme covers?
eligibility.no: Most bursaries need current enrolment. Apply to schools first, or look at NELFUND for public institutions.

eligibility.q: Does your institution type qualify (some states fund only public institutions)?
eligibility.no: Read your board's rules — Akwa Ibom's bursary is for public institutions, except students with disabilities who may attend any institution.

eligibility.q: Do you have a NIN that matches your school records?
eligibility.no: Enrol for or correct your NIN at NIMC first; boards like Akwa Ibom cross-check NIN with school records.

eligibility.q: Are you free from another government scholarship for the same session?
eligibility.no: Many boards (e.g. Akwa Ibom) bar double government funding. You may need to choose one.

eligibility.q: Do you meet any CGPA or age limit in your state's scheme?
eligibility.no: Check the rules: for example, Akwa Ibom's indigent-student scholarship asked for CGPA 3.5 and age under 25. If you miss a merit rule, apply for the need-based bursary instead.

steps.title: Find your state's official scholarship board
steps.why: Each state is different and scam sites copy state names. Finding the real board is step one.
do: Search '[your state] State Scholarship Board' and '[your state] bursary'.
Open only sites ending in .gov.ng or ones linked from your state government's official website (e.g. Lagos uses lagosscholarship.org, linked by the state).
Write down the board's address, phone number and social media handles.
If no website exists, visit the board office in your state capital or the Ministry of Education.
tips: Ask your school's Student Affairs office — they often receive state bursary circulars first.
Your state students' union (e.g. National Association of [State] Students) also shares verified updates.
avoid: Applying through blogs or WhatsApp links that ask for payment or bank PINs.
check: I have my board's official website or office address

steps.title: Learn which awards your state offers
steps.why: Boards run different schemes: need-based bursaries, merit scholarships, postgraduate awards, law school or special-needs bursaries. You must apply for the right one.
do: List each scheme your board runs and its level (undergraduate, ND/HND, NCE, Master's, PhD, Law School).
Note whether it is merit (CGPA/test) or need-based.
Note the amount and whether it is one-off or yearly.
Note any test or interview (Lagos uses oral and written assessments).
tips: You can sometimes apply for a bursary even if you miss the merit cut-off — read both.
avoid: Assuming last year's amounts still apply — check the current advert.
check: I know which scheme fits me

steps.title: Check you meet every rule
steps.why: Boards disqualify incomplete or ineligible applications without contacting you.
do: Answer each eligibility question above for your state.
Check CGPA, year of study and age rules in your scheme.
Check whether your institution type is accepted.
Plan a backup: NELFUND (public institutions), company scholarships, NDDC (Niger Delta states).
tips: If you are a Niger Delta indigene, also check NDDC and your state's oil-company-funded schemes.
avoid: Applying to a state where you only live but are not an indigene, unless the scheme says residents may apply.
check: I meet the rules for my chosen scheme

steps.title: Set reminders for your state's window
steps.why: Windows can be short — Lagos's 2025/26 window was about six weeks.
do: Note when your board opened last year.
Set calendar reminders to check its site and social media every two weeks from October.
Follow the board's official social media accounts.
Tell a friend from your state to alert you too.
tips: Apply in the first week — portals slow down near the deadline.
avoid: Relying only on blogs for dates.

steps.title: Get your certificate of origin (LGA letter)
steps.why: This is the core proof that you belong to the state. Some states also ask for a letter from your traditional ruler.
do: Go to your LGA secretariat (or its office in the state capital).
Bring your birth certificate, a passport photo and your parent's details.
Ask for a certificate of origin / LGA identification letter, signed and stamped.
If your state needs a traditional ruler's letter (Lagos asks for an Oba's letter), visit the palace with the same documents.
Scan both as PDF.
tips: Lagos applicants also need LASSRA registration — enrol early.
avoid: Using a certificate with a different name spelling from your NIN.
check: I have a signed certificate of origin (and ruler's letter if needed)

steps.title: Gather school documents
steps.why: Boards verify you are a current student and check your grades.
do: Download your admission letter and current session registration slip.
Get a copy of your student ID card.
Print your latest result showing CGPA (for merit awards ask for a signed transcript or statement).
Get your JAMB result slip and O'level results if asked.
Get a departmental testimonial letter if your scheme needs one (Akwa Ibom asked for it).
tips: Ask your HOD for the testimonial early; signatures take time.
avoid: Submitting results from a previous session as 'current'.
check: Admission letter, ID, result, registration slip ready

steps.title: Prepare ID, NIN and bank details
steps.why: Bursaries are paid into your own account and many portals verify NIN.
do: Print your NIN slip and check your name matches school records.
Confirm you have a personal bank account with BVN.
Take a recent passport photograph and save it as JPG.
If needed, get a letter stating your parents' occupation and income (for need-based awards).
tips: Keep all scans in one folder named by document type.
check: NIN, bank details and photo ready

steps.title: Write a short motivation or need statement (if asked)
steps.why: Some boards ask why you need support or how you will serve the state; it can decide close cases and guides your interview.
do: Check if your board asks for a letter or statement, and its limit.
Paragraph 1: who you are, course, level and CGPA.
Paragraph 2: your financial situation, honestly and briefly.
Paragraph 3: your goals and how you will contribute to your state.
Proofread and keep it to one page unless told otherwise.
tips: Give one concrete example of service: tutoring, community work, a project.
avoid: Exaggerating hardship — boards may verify it.
check: My statement is true, clear and within the limit
steps.prompt: Why you need the award and how you will contribute to your state (check your board's exact wording).
steps.limit: Check your board's guidance (one page is common)

steps.title: Get attestation or referee letters if required
steps.why: Some states ask for an attestation by a lecturer, community leader or public officer to confirm your identity and character.
do: Read the form to see who may sign (e.g. HOD, traditional ruler, LGA chairman).
Visit them with a printed copy of the form and your ID.
Make sure they sign, date and stamp it.
Scan the signed copy.
tips: Ask your HOD or a lecturer who knows you well.
avoid: Forging signatures — it is fraud and leads to disqualification.
check: Any required attestation is signed and stamped

steps.title: Apply on the official portal (or at the board office)
steps.why: Lagos advises completing the form in one session and reviewing before final submission; incomplete forms may be disqualified.
do: Open your board's official portal (e.g. portal.lagosscholarship.org for Lagos; bursary.akwaibomstate.gov.ng/auth/signup for Akwa Ibom).
If your state uses scratch cards or PINs, buy them only from the outlets the board names.
Sign up with your own email and phone; fill every section.
Upload each document in the right box.
Review, submit and save or print the acknowledgement.
tips: Use a laptop and stable internet; do it in one sitting.
avoid: Paying cyber-café agents who keep your login details.
check: I have an acknowledgement or application number

steps.title: Prepare for screening, test or interview
steps.why: Many boards screen documents in person and some run written or oral tests (Lagos does).
do: Watch the board's site and social media for screening dates.
Bring originals of every uploaded document.
For a test, revise English, maths and general knowledge about your state.
For an interview, practise saying your course, goals and how you will serve your state in under a minute.
avoid: Missing screening — absence usually means disqualification.
check: I know my screening date and have my originals

steps.title: Confirm payment and keep your award
steps.why: Payments can be delayed and some awards need yearly renewal and a minimum CGPA.
do: Check the published beneficiary list on the board's official site.
Check your bank account and keep any payment notice.
Read renewal rules (e.g. Akwa Ibom required keeping CGPA 3.5).
Set a reminder to re-apply or renew next session.
tips: Keep copies of your award letter for future applications.
avoid: Paying anyone who claims they can 'release' your bursary.
check: I know if I was selected and when payment comes

faq.q: I was born in Lagos but my parents are from Benue. Which state do I apply to?
faq.a: Usually your state of origin (Benue), shown on your LGA certificate. Some states allow long-term residents — read each board's rules.

faq.q: Do states pay for study abroad?
faq.a: Some do occasionally, but most current schemes are bursaries for study in Nigeria. Watch your board's site for special overseas calls.
Many portals are free (Akwa Ibom says it is free). Some boards use scratch cards — buy only from outlets they name.

faq.q: Can I hold a state bursary and NELFUND together?
faq.a: NELFUND is a loan, not a scholarship, but rules differ. Some boards bar other government scholarships — check your board's terms.

faq.q: How do I know a site is real?
faq.a: It ends in .gov.ng or is linked from your state government's official website or the board's verified social media.
